definitions.explanation: A large predatory fish with cartilaginous skeleton, multiple rows of teeth, and a streamlined body.

examples.japanese: {鮫|さめ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{海|うみ}→海：00556_umi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{食物連鎖|しょくもつれんさ}→食物連鎖：08437_shokumotsurensa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{頂点|ちょうてん}→頂点：05448_chouten⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: Sharks are at the top of the ocean food chain.

examples.english: Sharks have a highly developed sense of smell.

notes:
{鮫|さめ} refers to sharks in general.

Alternative writing: ⟦サメ→サメ：noentry⟧ (katakana, common in scientific contexts)

TYPES:
- ⟦ホホジロ→ホホジロ：noentry⟧{鮫|ざめ} / ⟦ホオジロ→ホオジロ：noentry⟧{鮫|ざめ} (great white shark)
- ⟦ジンベエ→ジンベエ：noentry⟧{鮫|ざめ} (whale shark)
- ⟦シュモク→シュモク：noentry⟧{鮫|ざめ} (hammerhead shark)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {鮫|さめ}⟦{肌|はだ}→肌：02243_hada⟧ (rough skin; literally "shark skin")
- {鮫|さめ}⟦{皮|がわ}→皮：02187_kawa⟧ (sharkskin, also used for sword handle wrapping)

COUNTING PATTERNS:
- ⟦{匹|ひき}→匹：00939_hiki⟧ or ⟦{頭|とう}→頭：18067_tou⟧ (for large sharks)

CULTURAL NOTE:
In traditional Japanese swordmaking, {鮫|さめ}⟦{皮|がわ}→皮：02187_kawa⟧ (ray/shark skin) is used to wrap sword handles for grip. This material is actually from rays rather than sharks in most cases.
